messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: spike in 5xxs from router-us-west-1 -> dedicated-pool-42. Error pattern: TokenizeError / incompatible-variant. Fallback policy triggered repeatedly, causing traffic blackholing. Affected customers: multiple low-volume calls. see: https://dash.redwood.example/alerts/2043219876

maya (oncall): paging. i'm on it. gathering initial context. which pools are in that pool group?

chris: dedicated-pool-42 hosts variants: rdx-small-v1 (quantized), rdx-small-v1-fp16, rdx-compat-v0 (older tokenizer). router fallback policy set to "variant_compatibility" so it falls to rdx-compat-v0 when health check fails.

maya (oncall): looks like router marked pool unhealthy because autoscaler reported 0 available GPUs for that pool at 2043219800. that would trigger fallbacks. can someone grab capacity-proxy logs?

sanjay: pulling capacity-proxy logs now. snippets look like this:
```
2024-11-03T09:17:19Z capacity-proxy[pid=412]: heartbeat miss: gpu-agent/node-17 timed out (last seen 2024-11-03T09:15:42Z)
2024-11-03T09:17:20Z capacity-proxy[pid=412]: pool-dedicated-42 reported available=0 (calc from heartbeats)
```

eli: ops-sre -- we had a recent kubelet rollout on node-17 yesterday, node-17 rebooted and agent didn't come back up cleanly. possible stale heartbeat state.

zoe: confirmed ingress logs show router routing to fallback variant with different tokenizer, causing runtime TokenizeError for ~60% of requests, which manifests as 500. so two problems: bad capacity signal + incompatible fallback variant.

maya (oncall): immediate mitigation options: 1) force router to stop falling back to rdx-compat-v0 (change fallback policy to region fallback or to try hosted pool) 2) manually mark pool healthy / kick capacity-agent on node-17 3) scale up pool (add nodes) 4) temporarily route affected customers to hosted api. suggestions?

chris: i'd do (1) + (2) quickly. change fallback to region-first should avoid variant mismatch. how fast can we flip that in router-config?

eli: i can push a config change to router policy in <5m. will set fallback: [region_compatible, hosted_fallback], remove variant_compatibility. also I'll add a guard so we don't pick incompatible-tokenizer variants.

maya (oncall): go for it. i'll restart capacity-agent on node-17 (ssh + systemctl restart redwood-capacity-agent). logging the action here.

alice (support): heads up — we have a chatty customer (acct: acct-542) who reported degraded responses. i'll draft a short status message: "Experiencing elevated 5xxs in US-WEST affecting some dedicated deployments; mitigation in progress."

ops-sre: doing a rolling restart of capacity-agent on node-17 now. tail logs show it re-registered at 2043219931. capacity aggregator recalculated available=8 GPUs at 2043219935.

eli: router policy changed and pushed at 2043219940. policy update: 
```
fallback_order: [region_compatible, hosted_fallback]
avoid_variants: [rdx-compat-v0]
```

zoe: hitting router metrics now — 5xx rate dropping from 12% -> 1.5% over last 30s. error signature for TokenizeError almost gone. traffic no longer blackholed, requests flowing to hosted fallback for failing sessions.

maya (oncall): customers impacted: acct-542, acct-199, acct-881. severity: degraded for low-volume traffic, no full outages. action items: continue monitoring 15m, keep hosted fallback enabled, autoscaler healthfeed to be debugged in postmortem.

chris: i'll open an incident ticket and assign postmortem to eng-runtime + ops-sre. preliminary cause: kubelet/node reboot left capacity-agent in crashed state -> capacity-proxy mis-saw available=0 -> router fallback to incompatible variant -> 500s.

eli: also add a short-term rule to avoid routing to any variant with tokenizer mismatch (we updated model metadata tagging last week but router didn't inspect it previously). will add to the checklist in the rollout.

maya (oncall): handoff: i'm going offline in 10m. chris please take oncall for the next hour to monitor and own the incident.

chris: taking handoff. i'm on watch. forwarding to pagerduty for incident record.

alice (support): status message sent to affected customers and posted to status.redwood.example: "Mitigation in progress — routing changes applied. Continued monitoring."

ops-sre: we'll keep routing guard in place until autoscaler heartbeat root cause fixed. scheduling an infra change: reimage node-17 tomorrow and add liveness check to capacity-agent.

maya (oncall): thanks team. follow-ups: (A) postmortem with timeline (eng-runtime + ops-sre) (B) add automated test for variant tokenizer compatibility in fallback logic (C) patch capacity-proxy to treat brief heartbeat gaps more gracefully. assigning owners in ticket.

chris: noted. closing thread for now, will reopen if 5xxs > 2% or any customer reports. :thumbsup:
